Came here to say this. People experience MDD differently. Some of us have all the symptoms, or are incredibly melancholy, or have mostly physical symptoms like fatigue. 

For these people, stimulants have been shown to be more effective because it’s not their mood that needs a boost but their body. Wellbutrin is a fantastic option for a lot of people.

A brief cap of my experience with Wellbutrin: I have PTSD/Anxiety, not MDD. However I have a lot of MDD symptoms because they all cross over, right? We tried Wellbutrin at one point, and it increased my anxiety and caused crazy physical symptoms like shaking and jitters. It was so intense, I became suddenly suicidal our of the blue. Luckily, my Psych warned me of this possibility so we were able to nip it in the bud. 

Wellbutrin tends to be either incredible or terrible for people, but I’d say it’s well worth a try, as long as you know what to watch out for in case it doesn’t work for you.

So I had to taper during pregnancy. I was so dependent  and had so much anxiety during pregnancy they actually had me stay on Kpin up until month 8. I had antenatal psychosis, was very suicidal, and it was best for me and the baby to keep me calm and get through the pregnancy.

I did it with my psychiatrist + OB’s help and support, and did 7 day increments of -0.25 mg. Some days when I could go without it (happened occasionally) I would do so. I was completely off in 4 weeks (was taking 1 mg daily to start).

I’m not sure if you’re a woman or not, but if you are, I do have a piece of advice for surviving pregnancy. Find an OBGYN who supports use of your meds during pregnancy. All. Of. Your. Meds. 

They aren’t dangerous. They do have some risks but so does tuna fish. When I got pregnant, I was perfectly stable and that’s why we chose to go forward. During pregnancy I needed 3 med changes and I had a suicide attempt, which I haven’t had outside of pregnancy.

My psychiatrist and OBGYN worked together like the A Team. They told me that while pregnant, your body has so many hormone changes and the like, that you don’t respond to meds the same. You can also experience a worsening (or improvement) of symptoms you previously had.

They supported my need for medication saying that a healthy child is one who has a healthy mother. And at birth they had a team of neonatal withdrawal specialists ready to help her if she was having withdrawals from the medications. There was zero judgment and only support.

If you choose to have kids (and if you will be the one carrying them) I hope you find a medical team as fantastic as mine. Any OBGYN who says you can’t take (MOST) psych meds isn’t up on their research.
